title: Antarctica's Ice Hit Minus 135 Degrees, Seen From Space

scenes.text: Somewhere in Antarctica, the ice hit minus 135 degrees.
Nobody was there with a thermometer. Satellites caught it.
It happened on August tenth, 2010, on a high ridge, and scientists found it by combining 32 years of satellite data.
The old record, set at Vostok Station in 1983, was minus 128.6 degrees.
This new low is about seven degrees colder, and it happens in hollows on winter nights.
So the coldest place on Earth was measured from space.

description:
Somewhere in Antarctica the ice surface hit minus 135.8 degrees Fahrenheit.
Satellites measured it on August 10, 2010, about seven degrees colder than the old Vostok record of minus 128.6.
Could you last one minute out there?
first_comment: Minus 135.8 degrees. What is the coldest day you have ever lived through?
